arrange.copyStyleTip: Take the style from the last-selected object: panels give crop / rotation / opacity, text gives size / weight / colour / alignment
arrange.createLayoutTip: Turn the selection into a {{kind}} layout: fixed spacing, arranged automatically, and re-flowed after an asset swap (undoable)
arrange.dissolveTitle: Remove the layout constraints and grouping; object positions stay as they are
arrange.groupTip: Once grouped, clicking any member selects and moves the whole group
arrange.pasteStyleEmpty: No style has been copied yet
arrange.pasteStyleTip: Paste onto the {{kind}} in the selection

refTip.page: Use the whole canvas as the reference
refTip.primary: Use the last-selected object as the reference; it stays put
refTip.selection: Use the selection's bounding box as the reference

arrange.reflowTitle: Re-flow every member with the current constraints
arrange.spacingHTitle: Horizontal spacing: sorted by X and packed in order; the first object stays put
arrange.spacingVTitle: Vertical spacing: sorted by Y and packed in order; the first object stays put
arrange.ungroupTip: Break up the groups in the selection

autoHideAria: Right panel auto-hides; click to pin it
autoHideTip: Auto-hiding: collapses when the selection is cleared. Click to pin it open.

single.hint: 85 mm — single-column width at most journals
single.label: Single column

canvas.safeAreaTip: Only a reference frame on the canvas — it never crops and never affects the export
canvas.snapObjectsTip: Page edges and centre lines always snap; hold {{mod}} while dragging to disable snapping temporarily

control.legendCustomHint: The legend was dragged to a custom spot; pick any preset (including Best fit) to snap back.
control.aspectRatio: Aspect ratio value: display length of one Y unit over one X unit
control.resetDiagram_one: Reset ticks and frame to script ({{count}} item)
control.resetDiagram_other: Reset ticks and frame to script ({{count}} items)
control.legendPreviewAria: Position preview: the container bounds and where the legend sits
control.legendOutsideOverflowHint: Placing it outside may run past the figure; the checks will say so.

element.absentAppearance: Visible in the figure, but this version can't edit it here — it comes from the script.
element.alignHint: For axes this changes their share of the figure (matplotlib position); for text and legends it moves the anchor. Neither affects the panel's size on the canvas.
element.alignHintAnnotations: Canvas annotations line up on the same baseline; their position changes on the canvas object.
element.alignHintGroup: Dragging the group's bounding-box handles on the canvas scales it too.
element.alignInvalid: An element in the selection has invalid geometry; this alignment was cancelled.
element.alignNoop: These elements are already aligned; nothing to change.
element.alignRefLastTip: {{tip}} · uses the last selected element as reference
element.alignSyncing: Syncing the in-figure layout — alignment is available in a moment.
element.backToScriptPartial_one: Back to the script value ({{count}} changed)
element.backToScriptPartial_other: Back to the script value ({{count}} changed)
element.batchHint_one: Changes apply to the {{count}} selected element
element.batchHint_other: Changes apply to all {{count}} selected elements
element.batchNoCommon: These elements have no properties that can be changed together
element.clickToEdit: Click an element in the figure to start editing

hint.scatterSize: pt² is an area, not a diameter: doubling the value makes the dot about 1.4× wider.

element.howAiBody: Rewrites the .py script itself. A snapshot is taken before every run, so the task history can "Revert this change".
element.howBothBody: After the script changes, figure edits pointing at elements that no longer exist are skipped and flagged in the problems panel; the rest still apply.
element.howOverrideBody: Saved in this document — neither the script nor the figure on disk changes. They can be undone; "Restore this element" / "Restore the whole figure" clear them in one step. Exports re-render at full quality.
element.howWriteBackBody: This is the only step that overwrites the figure on disk. It is backed up first, and "History" can return to any version.
element.howWriteBackTitle: Write back to the original file
element.keptPrevious: The previous image is still shown

numberList.empty: This axis has no ticks right now

element.openSourceAdvanced: Change it in the source file
element.proxiedGeometry: Position and size apply to the host axes “{{label}}”.
element.resetDiagram: Reset ticks and frame to script
element.scaleTitle: Scales about the centre; relative layout inside the group is preserved
element.textBatchHintMixed_one: These elements differ in kind, so only the text styles they all support are listed; edits apply to {{count}} element.
element.textBatchHintMixed_other: These elements differ in kind, so only the text styles they all support are listed; edits apply to all {{count}}.
element.waiting: Waiting for the engine to render…
element.colorScaleTip: The colormap and the scale limits are one state: change either side and the other follows.

emptyHint: Click a panel, text or annotation on the canvas to start editing.
hideElementTip: Hide this element (restorable at any time)
overlayTip: The window is narrow, so the right panel shows as an overlay. Widen the window to pin it.

panel.aspectLocked: Aspect ratio locked — changing one side changes the other
panel.aspectTip: Keep the width and fix the height to the original ratio (removes stretching)
panel.aspectUnlocked: Aspect ratio unlocked — W and H are independent
panel.bitmapBoth: Both flipping and opacity make this panel embed as a bitmap in the exported PDF — vector text will no longer be selectable.
panel.bitmapFlip: Flipped panels embed as a bitmap at export DPI in the PDF; vector text is no longer selectable.
panel.bitmapOpacity: Below 100% opacity, this panel embeds as a high-resolution bitmap in the exported PDF; vector text is no longer selectable.
panel.coldBuilding: Cold start in progress; this can take a few minutes…
panel.cropCancelTip: Restore the framing from when you entered crop (Esc)
panel.cropTip: Drag the crop frame on the canvas to reframe
panel.dpiHint: The bitmap's actual resolution at the current size
panel.dpiHintBad: Below 300dpi — this will look soft in print
panel.fillTip: Keep the frame; crop centrally to cut off the overflow
panel.fitTip: Scale the whole image into the current frame; the frame shrinks to the image's ratio
panel.nativeSizeTip: Back to the asset's own mm size (100% scale)
panel.nativeTip: The asset's own size is {{w}}×{{h}} cm; scale % is always relative to it
panel.nativeTipMulti: The asset's own size; scale % is always relative to it
panel.ptHintBad: {{base}}pt in the original × {{scale}}% scale — below 6pt is unreadable in print
panel.replaceDescription: Position, size, crop, rotation and stacking order are kept. Figure edits cannot move across scripts, so you will be asked before they are cleared.
panel.replaceTip: Keeps position, size, crop and stacking order; only swaps the image source
panel.rotationTip: Only 90° steps: the compositor cannot fill the target frame at other angles
panel.scaleTitle: Absolute percentage of the original size: 100% = original. Cropping does not change the reference.
panel.sourceHint: Writing back overwrites the original PDF/PNG file. A backup is kept so you can restore it.
panel.staleScript: The script changed — entering edit mode rebuilds it automatically

pinnedAria: Right panel is pinned; click to auto-hide it
pinnedTip: Pinned: stays open even with nothing selected. Click to auto-hide instead.

sync.clampedNote_one: ({{count}} position was refitted to the target layout and may need a tweak)
sync.clampedNote_other: ({{count}} positions were refitted to the target layout and may need a tweak)
sync.mergeToCanvas: Merge into the panel on the canvas
sync.noOverrides: This panel has no figure edits yet
sync.notOnCanvas: The target figure is not on the canvas, so it can only be written straight back to its original file (merged with its existing baseline, backed up automatically). To see the result first, drop it onto the canvas and sync again.
sync.nothingToSync: Nothing to sync; you can cancel.
sync.onlyOne: This script only produces one figure
sync.skippedSuffix: items — layout geometry (axes box / figure size) cannot move between figures
sync.syncAndWriteBack: Sync and write back to the original file
sync.syncedToCanvas_one: Synced {{count}} edit to {{name}} on the canvas
sync.syncedToCanvas_other: Synced {{count}} edits to {{name}} on the canvas
sync.tip: Map the current figure edits onto other figures from the same script (composite ↔ sub-figure works both ways; the direction follows whichever you start from)
sync.title: Sync edits
sync.unmatchedSuffix: items — these elements do not exist in the target figure
sync.writtenBack: Synced and written back to the original file: {{name}}

text.glyphFallback: These characters are drawn with a different font: {{chars}}
text.glyphMissing: These characters cannot be drawn and export as boxes: {{chars}}
text.interpretationAutoTip: Synthesize super/subscripts only for characters that cannot be drawn (default); everything else is left as typed
text.interpretationScientificTip: Synthesize every recognized Unicode super/subscript: one consistent font, but copying from the exported PDF gives 105 instead of 10⁵
text.matchHint: Body text in the figure renders at about {{eff}}pt
text.matchTitle: Annotation size is absolute on the page. With “{{panel}}” scaled to {{scale}}%, {{base}}pt body text inside the figure renders at about {{eff}}pt. Use this value to match it.
text.newlineTitle: Insert a line break at the cursor (on-canvas editing also takes {{alt}} / {{mod}})
text.subscriptTitle: Subscript: select a range in the text box, then click ({{key}})
text.superscriptTitle: Superscript: select a range in the text box, then click ({{key}})
text.title: Text

textActions.newlineTitle: Insert a line break at the cursor ({{alt}} / {{mod}})
textActions.subTitle: Subscript: select a range, then click — written as a matplotlib expression (H$_{2}$O)
textActions.supTitle: Superscript: select a range, then click — written as a matplotlib expression (cm$^{-1}$)

textControls.fontMissingHint: This computer does not have that font, so the figure is actually drawn with a different one. Pick an available font, or install it.

transform.textHeightAuto: Text height is determined by the content
transform.title: Position and size

unsupported.child_axes_locator: This child axes is positioned by its parent on every frame; a change here would snap back on the next draw
unsupported.multi_host_colorbar: This colorbar spans {{hosts}} subplots; switching its orientation is not supported in this version
unsupported.parasite_host_draw: This is a parasite axes from host_subplot; the host draws its contents and never checks this switch — hide the individual elements on it instead
unsupported.parasite_host_rect: This is a parasite axes from host_subplot; its position is reset by the host on every draw — move the host subplot and it follows along
unsupported.unknown: Changing this here is not supported in this version
unsupported.legend_anchor_box: The script anchors this legend to a rectangle (four numbers); only legends anchored to a single point can be edited here
unsupported.legend_anchor_transform: The script pins this legend's anchor to a different coordinate system; only legends anchored to their own container can be edited here

versionHistory.originWarn: "Script original" re-renders from the script's current output — it does not restore the original file's bytes. If the original was hand-edited, or the script changed since, the result will differ from the original file and only the backup folder has it.
versionHistory.restoreTip: Rewrite the original file from this version
versionHistory.restored: Restored this version and rewrote the original (backup in {{dir}})
versionHistory.warnBody: This rewrites the original file from this version's edits (backed up automatically to cache/original_backups).
versionHistory.warnForward: History only moves forward: this restore is appended as a new entry, so you can always change your mind again.

writeBack.annotationsTitle: Canvas arrows, text and shapes lying on the panel are drawn as vectors into the original PDF at their current positions (the PNG is re-rendered to match), then removed from the canvas (undoable)
writeBack.backupDone: The originals were backed up to {{dir}} — expand for how to restore
writeBack.backupSummary: Backed up to {{dir}} before overwriting — expand for how to restore
writeBack.buttonLabel: Write back to the original file
writeBack.confirm: Write back to the original files
writeBack.divergenceBody: : the current editing state does not match a clean replay (what you would get after reopening the project). The original file was left untouched. This is an engine-level problem — please report the details below to the developers.
writeBack.hasOverridesTitle: Overwrite the original PDF/PNG in figures with the current figure edits
writeBack.noOverridesTitle: There are no figure edits to write back yet
writeBack.readOnlyTitle: This project has “Allow writing back to original files” turned off; turn it on in project settings
writeBack.restoreBody: Restore: the panel’s “History” can return to any version, or you can copy files back from the backup folder directly. The script that generates the figure is never modified.
writeBack.scriptChanged: The script {{script}} changed during this editing session, so what you see is still the old code. Re-render the panel, check the result, then write back.
writeBack.sizeMismatch: The page size after write-back does not match the replay. The file has been replaced and the original is still in the backup folder — check it, restore from the backup if needed, and report this to the developers.
writeBack.sourceChanged: The asset {{file}} was changed outside this tool. Reload the figure library to see its current contents, then write back again.
writeBack.statusPlain: Written back to the original files: {{files}} (backup in {{dir}})
writeBack.statusWithAnnotations_one: Written back to the original files: {{files}} (including {{count}} annotation; backup in {{dir}})
writeBack.statusWithAnnotations_other: Written back to the original files: {{files}} (including {{count}} annotations; backup in {{dir}})
writeBack.summaryMany_one: Writing {{count}} figure edit back into the original files of {{panels}} figures
writeBack.summaryMany_other: Writing {{count}} figure edits back into the original files of {{panels}} figures
writeBack.summaryOne_one: Writing {{count}} figure edit back into the original files of “{{stem}}”
writeBack.summaryOne_other: Writing {{count}} figure edits back into the original files of “{{stem}}”
writeBack.targetsLabel: These files in the figures folder will be overwritten
writeBack.title: Write back to the original file
writeBack.topBarMany_one: Write back to the original files: {{count}} panel
writeBack.topBarMany_other: Write back to the original files: {{count}} panels
writeBack.topBarOne: Write back to the original file: {{stem}}
writeBack.topBarReadOnly: This project has “Allow writing back to original files” turned off; turn it on in project settings
writeBack.verified_one: Verified against a clean replay ({{count}} element matched)
writeBack.verified_other: Verified against a clean replay ({{count}} elements matched)
writeBack.withAnnotations_one: Write the canvas annotation back too ({{count}})
writeBack.withAnnotations_other: Write the canvas annotations back too ({{count}})

legend.followHint: The handle is derived from that object in the figure. Unlink to give it its own colour, line style and marker.
legend.customHint: The handle is no longer derived from the figure object. Relinking restores the derived look.
legend.customHintStyled: The handle uses the style you set here. Relinking undoes those changes in one step.
legend.spacingUnitNote: In font-size units: 1 em = one legend font size.
